title: i0jtaq
The Event of Mubahala and the Trust of the Ahl al-Bayt
hook: The Prophet brought out the Ahl al-Bayt for the mubahala. He left the Book and the itra (his kin) as a trust, so that they would not be separated.
scenes.0.text: One morning, the Prophet left his house to meet a delegation of Christians from Necran. The Necrans were claiming that Jesus was the son of God. The Prophet said he was a servant of Allah and a prophet, but the dispute was not resolved. Then the 61st verse of Surah al-Imran came down and called the two sides to quarrel. The two parties will say, "The curse of Allah be on the one who is a liar". The verse wanted both sides to bring their sons, their wives and themselves. The Prophet did not come to this call with an army. He was accompanied only by **Ali**, his daughter **Fatima** and their grandchildren **Hasan** and Husayn. When the Necranians saw the faces of these five, they dared not curse each other and agreed to make a deal.

scenes.1.text: The Prophet was commanded to bring his sons, his wives and himself. The Prophet brought Hasan and Husayn instead of his sons and Fatimah instead of his wives. And in return for saying "ourselves", he had **Ali** with him. So the Prophet put Ali in his own place, his own life. This was not just about taking him in as an uncle's son or son-in-law. The Necranians saw two separate people that day, but the verse identified them as one soul. In Tebek, the Prophet (peace be upon him) compared Ali to Aaron. And at Mubahele, he considered it his own life. The Shiites base the guardianship of Ali on this closeness.

scenes.2.text: On their way back from the Hajj, the caravan stopped at the Hum water between Mecca and Medina. The Prophet said that he had left behind two heavy trusts for his people: the Book of Allah and the Itrāh, or the People of the House. He repeatedly said, "I will remember God for my household". He said these two trusts would not be parted until they met the Prophet at the Pool. The pool is the pool of the Day of Judgment. Years later, Zeid b. Erkam was asked who the Ahl al-Bayt were. Zeid kept the Prophet's wives out of this close circle and counted the families of Ali, Aqil, Jafer and Abbas. The Prophet took his family with him so that the Qur'an could be understood.

scenes.3.text: The Prophet used another parable to describe the people of the House: "The example of the people of the House is like the Ark of Noah. Whoever rides it will survive, and whoever is left of it will drown". It's called Safine's Hadith. Safine means ship. The Flood of Noah's day was a global flood, and only those inside the ark survived. In this hadith, the flood is the division and confusion in which the Ummah will fall after the Prophet. And the ship of salvation in that storm is the Ehl-i-Beit. The Shiites believe that one must hold on to this ship to stay on course after the Prophet.
scenes.4.text: Sahaba Jabir b. Samura was with the Prophet one day. The Prophet said, "This religion will remain until there are twelve caliphs among you". Then he lowered his voice so that he could not hear a sentence. He asked his father what the Prophet said. His father said he said, "They're all from Quraysh". This hadith goes for Buhari and Muslim. Sunni scholars give different lists of who these twelve were. The Shia reading fills this number with twelve imams of the Ahl al-Bayt. The number given by the Prophet coincides exactly with the twelve imams, beginning with Ali and ending with Mahdi.

scenes.5.text: In the stories of the people of the House, Jabir b. An incident involving Abdullah is also related. Jabir saw a plaque next to **Fatima**. On the tablet were written the names of the imams who would come after the Prophet. The first name on the sign was **Ali**. Then came the sons of Fatima, **Hasan** and Husayn. His last name was the Mahdi, who would appear in the last days. According to this tradition, the names of the imams were determined before they were even born.

scenes.6.text: ==The Imamate== is the leadership in the Shia faith that is established by Allah with a clear declaration. That's an open declaration called a **nass**. The Imam is protected by Allah and is above all in knowledge. According to the Shiites, the earth will never be empty of an imam who has the Hajj of Allah, the proof of guidance for mankind. Every imam clearly announces what will come after him. In the meantime, it's not up to the people to play or choose. The Prophet had shown the first ring of this line, Ali, in front of everyone. In Sakife, this election was set aside, but the line of imams never broke.

scenes.7.text: The Twelve Imams of the Shi'a are as follows: **Ali**, **Hasan**, Husayn, Zayn al-Abidin, Muhammad Bakr, Ja'fer-i Sadik, Musa Qasim, **Ali Rıza**, Muhammad Taki, **Ali Nakis**, Hasan Asker and **Mehdi**. This chain didn't break even when Husayn was martyred in Karbala. His sick son, Zeynal Abidin, survived and the imamate continued with him. Subsequent imams lived in classrooms in Medina, in dungeons and under surveillance in Baghdad and Samarra. The 12th Imam, the Mahdi, is in the dark. The unseen is not death, but concealment. The Shiites believe that when the time comes, he will be brought to justice.

sunni.0.says: When the verse of mubahala was revealed, the Prophet called Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn and said, "O God, these are my family."
sunni.1.says: Two weighty trusts at the waters of Khumm: the Book of God and the Ahl al-Bayt; debate over its scope.
sunni.2.says: The Book and the itra will not be separated until they reach the Prophet at the Hawd.
sunni.3.says: The people of the House are like Noah's Ark. The Judge will give the verdict of peace.
sunni.3.grade: Al-Hakim: sahih; some hadith scholars consider it weak (disputed)
sunni.4.says: Jabir b. Samura: "There will be twelve amirs"; his father says, "All of them are from Quraysh."
sunni.5.says: Jabir b. Samura: "This caliphate will continue until twelve caliphs have come"; all of them are from Quraysh.
shia.0.says: Imamate is by nass, the hujja will never be lacking, and the narration of the tablet that Jabir saw with Lady Fatima.
shia.1.says: Narrations giving the names of the twelve imams, and the occultation.
shia.2.says: Narrations from the Prophet about twelve caliphs/imams; the occultation of the twelfth imam.
shia.3.says: The chains of the Safina hadith in Shia and Sunni sources, and al-Hakim's ruling of authenticity.
shia.4.says: The transmission of the tablet hadith in al-Kafi, Kamal al-Din and al-Nu'mani's al-Ghayba; al-Barqi's criticism.
disputes.0.title: mog26s
Who is "ourselves" in the mubahala?
disputes.0.sunni: The Prophet brought out Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn to the mubahala; this is a great merit. In the Sunni reading, the verse gives no ruling about the caliphate.
disputes.0.shia: The Prophet brought out Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn to the mubahala; this is a great merit. In Shia thought, the word "anfusana" (ourselves) makes Ali the self of the Prophet and shows his unique position.
disputes.1.title: 11lfo4i
Thaqalayn: "my itra" or "my sunna"?
disputes.1.sunni: In Muslim and Tirmidhi, the Prophet leaves the trust of "the Book and the itra." In the Sunni reading, the wording "the Book and my sunna" is also narrated; the saying means love and respect for the Ahl al-Bayt and is not counted as proof of imamate.
disputes.1.shia: In Muslim and Tirmidhi, the Prophet leaves the trust of "the Book and the itra." In Shia thought, this wording is authentic; that they are not separated from the Qur'an shows that the Ahl al-Bayt are the measure in religion.
disputes.2.title: kqg6ik
The authenticity of the Safina hadith
disputes.2.sunni: Al-Hakim relates the Safina hadith from Abu Dharr in al-Mustadrak. Although al-Hakim calls it sahih, some hadith scholars find its chains weak.
disputes.2.shia: Al-Hakim relates the Safina hadith from Abu Dharr in al-Mustadrak. In Shia thought, because it has come through many routes, it is regarded as certain in meaning.
disputes.3.title: qzqwdl
Who are the "twelve caliphs"?
disputes.3.sunni: Bukhari and Muslim mention twelve amirs or twelve caliphs; all are from Quraysh and the hadith names no one. In the Sunni reading, this number is explained by the first caliphs, the Umayyad caliphs, or future just rulers; a matching of names with the twelve imams does not exist in these sources.
disputes.3.shia: Bukhari and Muslim mention twelve amirs or twelve caliphs; all are from Quraysh and the hadith names no one. In Shia thought, the number corresponds to the Twelve Imams; al-Kafi, al-Ghayba and Kamal al-Din report the names, while some Shia scholars such as al-Barqi have criticized the tablet narration in terms of text and chain.
questions.0: Prophet Necran appeared before the delegation with Ali, Fatima, Hasan and Husayn. Why do you think the Prophet took these four people with him?
questions.1: The Prophet left the Book with the people of the House. Why do you think the Prophet entrusted the Book not to himself but to the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.2: Buhari and Muslim have the number "twelve". The Shi'a meet this number with the names of the Twelve Imams. Why do you think we need names for the meaning of a number?
questions.3: He compares the Companions of the House to Noah's Ark. Why do you think the Prophet compared the Ahl al-Bayt specifically to Noah's Ark?
summary: The words Mubahele, two amanah, and twelve caliphs indicate the location of the Ahl-i Bayt. These are also mentioned in Sunni sources (Muslim, Sahih; Tirmizi, al-Jâmi', no. 3788; Buhari, Sahih, no. 7222; Muslim, Sahih, no. 1821). The Shi'a consider these as evidence of the divine appointment of Ali and the Twelve Imams from his lineage.
key: Mubahala: the Prophet brought only the Ahl al-Bayt with him
notes.0: The mubahala is a call to mutual cursing made with the Christian delegation of Najran (Âl-i İmrân 3:61).
notes.1: The Prophet brought Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn with him.
notes.2: The people of Najran shrank from mutual cursing and accepted the agreement.
notes.3: The Prophet said, on the return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, that he was leaving the Book and the Ahl al-Bayt as a trust (Muslim 2408, Tirmidhi 3788).
notes.4: The "twelve caliphs" hadith is read as referring to the imams of the Ahl al-Bayt.
